# Backpressure

Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate, rather than letting an unbounded buffer grow until the process runs out of memory.

## Common Implementations

### Bounded Queues

The producer is blocked once the queue reaches capacity. This forces the producer to wait until the consumer processes items and makes room in the queue.

### Credit-Based Flow Control

The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items. The producer only emits up to the available credit, and the consumer issues new credit as it processes items.

### Reactive Pull Model

Instead of the producer pushing items to the consumer, the consumer requests items on its own schedule. This inverts the control flow: the consumer pulls items as it is ready to process them.
